title: What If You Never Slept? 🧠
description:
Tonight, you stop sleeping. Forever.
Your brain loses its night shift: no rinse cycle, no saving memories, and tiny parts of it start falling asleep anyway. Dolphins have a clever trick for this.

What would you do with a third of your life back? Tell us in the comments.

#shorts #science #brain #sleep #whatif
facts_checked: We spend about one third of our lives asleep -> https://www.ninds.nih.gov/Disorders/Patient-Caregiver-Education/Understanding-Sleep ; https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/12148-sleep-basics

In deep (slow-wave) sleep, waves of cerebrospinal fluid wash through the brain about every 20 s -> https://alzforum.org/node/1256466 (Fultz et al., Science 2019) ; https://www.news-medical.net/news/20191031/Sleep-protects-the-brain-against-Alzheimers-by-washing-it.aspx

Sleep may clear waste/toxins from the brain (said as 'scientists think') -> https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/10/131017144636.htm (NIH-funded, Science 2013) ; https://www.ninds.nih.gov/Disorders/Patient-Caregiver-Education/Understanding-Sleep

During sleep the hippocampus replays the day's experiences to consolidate memories -> https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/making-memories-during-sleep-takes-longer-expected ; https://www.ninds.nih.gov/Disorders/Patient-Caregiver-Education/Understanding-Sleep

Losing sleep raises waste protein (beta-amyloid) and harms new memory formation -> https://www.nih.gov/news-events/nih-research-matters/sleep-deprivation-increases-alzheimers-protein ; https://www.ninds.nih.gov/Disorders/Patient-Caregiver-Education/Understanding-Sleep

When sleep deprived, specific brain regions fall asleep locally while the person is awake -> https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2017/11/171108124201.htm ; https://english.tau.ac.il/node/2250 (Nir et al., Nature Medicine 2017)
Microsleeps last seconds and can happen with eyes open -> https://www.sleepfoundation.org/how-sleep-works/microsleep ; https://health.clevelandclinic.org/what-you-should-know-about-microsleep

Dolphins sleep with one half of the brain at a time and stay alert -> https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/dolphins-sleep-with-only-half-their-brain-at-a-time-81426439/ ; https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/10/121017181244.htm
